fixes.detail: falls_sheet renders as an opaque brown 10 m pillar that reads as a timber post. Make it emissive white-teal (or a translucent sheet with the pool_uplight raking it). Raise lights1:1 to about 3x lights1:0 and lights1:2 so the centre fall is the brightest thing on the ledge.

Six 1.6 m lantern_stone at almost even 8-10 m intervals, offset 2.4 m on the sea side. They are the brightest objects and pull the eye away from the falls. Replace the 'along spine' rule with pairs flanking each basin (x 152.5/157.5, 170.5/175.5, 188.5/193.5) plus the stair foot, leaving dark gaps between.
Sea-rail posts every 10-11 m make a second even row parallel to lights[0]. Use spacing [12,18] and skip posts within 3 m of the pines (162, 186), so the pines read as silhouettes against the surf.

All three cameras pitch 40-65 deg up. Lower the targets: entry (172,108,6), reveal (176,108,10), concept (165,108,12). Keep the ledge, basin and falls in the bottom third and the stacked suites above.
boulder_rim at z -0.65 with h 0.7 is almost fully sunk. Raise it to z -0.22 like its siblings. Same for dressing4:2 (z -0.62) and dressing5:2 (z -0.39), or remove them.

top_change: The ledge is 11 m deep at the foot of a 63 m near-vertical cliff, so the lit suite fronts can't be seen from it at eye height. Set each suite tier back 4-6 m into the cliff (a stepped elevation, as image 32 shows), or add a sea-stack lookout or jetty 30-40 m north, so the suite elevation becomes visible.
plausibility: Upward cameras show balcony soffits only. With tiers stacked plumb, the lit shoji fronts are geometrically invisible from the ledge.
Several boulder_rim stones are sunk 0.4-0.65 m (dressing3:0, dressing4:2, dressing5:2).
Hero falls_sheet spans z -1.2 to 8.8 and ends 1.2 m below the tier-1 floor (z 10). Check that the gully trickle above continues down to meet it, so there is no visible gap.
Railings along the sea edge are not visible in any render (structural, z 1.05).
